top_helpful_lessons.text: Provide a pinpoint citation (document name and section/clause) for every issue, factual assertion, or proposed amendment. If no citation exists, state 'Not addressed in [document name].'
Adopt a consistent risk rating scale (e.g., High/Medium/Low) for all issues. Define the criteria for each rating in the methodology section of the deliverable.
When identifying notice periods or deadlines, check for conflicts between documents. Recommend the most conservative approach or alignment to protect client interests.
Assign a standardised risk rating (High/Medium/Low) to every issue. Use a consistent format (e.g., '**Risk Rating: High**') and justify the rating in the analysis.
For every identified issue, provide an explicit, actionable recommendation. Specify the exact remedy (e.g., 'amend Clause X to Y' or 'obtain a ratifying resolution').
For every inconsistency between related provisions across documents, explicitly flag it as a separate issue. Include a recommendation for harmonisation or further review.
Review all restrictive covenants across transaction documents and employment agreements. Identify and flag inconsistencies in scope, duration, or enforceability under relevant jurisdiction law.

Create a dedicated section for required approvals, conditions precedent, or third-party consents. List each item and explicitly state its status (e.g., 'not validly obtained,' 'missing,' 'pending') and the legal consequence (e.g., 'invalid,' 'unenforceable,' 'requires ratification').

Before finalizing an issues list, ensure every issue includes: (1) a pinpoint citation, (2) an explicit risk rating, (3) an actionable recommendation, (4) flags for inconsistencies between related provisions, and (5) enforceability assessments for restrictive covenants. Recommend legal advice if enforceability is uncertain.
For every calculation or derived figure, specify its source: client-provided data, document-extracted data, or assumptions. Flag any uncertainties or limitations.
